towns.name: Laoag City
towns.title: The Sunshine City of the North & Capital of Ilocos Norte
towns.description: Laoag City is the vibrant capital of Ilocos Norte, rich in Spanish colonial architecture, cultural heritage landmarks, and bustling commercial districts.

towns.name: Paoay
towns.title: Home of the UNESCO World Heritage Paoay Church
towns.description: Famous for the majestic Saint Augustine Church (Paoay Church), Paoay Lake, historical presidential residences, and thrilling sand dune adventures.

towns.name: Pagudpud
towns.title: The Boracay of the North & Eco-Tourism Haven
towns.description: Renowned for pristine white sand beaches, Saud Beach, Blue Lagoon, and scenic coastal mountain ranges.

towns.name: Adams
towns.title: The Eco-Tourism Paradise in the Mountains
towns.description: Nestled amidst lush rainforests and waterfalls, home to diverse indigenous cultural communities and eco-adventures.

towns.name: Bacarra
towns.title: Home of the Beheading Belfry
towns.description: Known for its historical ruined bell tower damaged by earthquakes and rich agricultural traditions.

towns.name: Badoc
towns.title: Birthplace of Juan Luna & Sanctuary of La Virgen Milagrosa
towns.description: Historic town featuring the Juan Luna Shrine and the Minor Basilica of La Virgen Milagrosa de Badoc.

towns.name: Bangui
towns.title: Pioneer of Wind Energy in Southeast Asia
towns.description: Iconic destination famous for the giant Bangui Windmills along Bangui Bay.

towns.name: Banna
towns.title: Rice & Agriculture Hub
towns.description: Celebrated for rice production, traditional crafts, and peaceful countryside scenery.

towns.name: Burgos
towns.title: Home of Cape Bojeador Lighthouse & Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
towns.description: Stunning coastal landscapes, natural white limestone cliffs, and historic lighthouse built in 1892.

towns.name: Carasi
towns.title: Nature & River Sanctuary
towns.description: Quiet upland town known for clear river systems, waterfalls, and eco-trekking routes.

towns.name: Currimao
towns.title: Port Town & Coral Rock Formations
towns.description: Features calm beaches, ancient coral rock formations, and port facilities.

towns.name: Dingras
towns.title: Rice Granary of Ilocos Norte
towns.description: Agricultural powerhouse with historic brick church ruins of St. Joseph Parish.

towns.name: Dumalneg
towns.title: Cultural Ancestral Domain
towns.description: Home to indigenous Isnag communities preserving rich traditional customs.

towns.name: Marcos
towns.title: Lush Valleys & Eco-Farm Sites
towns.description: Known for agricultural productivity, caves, and scenic valley hills.

towns.name: Nueva Era
towns.title: Tingguian Heritage & Eco-Cultural Park
towns.description: Cultural destination celebrating Tingguian indigenous traditions and mountain resort experiences.

towns.name: Pasuquin
towns.title: Salt Capital & Biscotcho Delicacy Hub
towns.description: Famous for coastal salt-making farms and the delicious Ilocano biscotcho pastry.

towns.name: Piddig
towns.title: Home of Basi Revolt & Coffee Capital
towns.description: Historical town famous for the 1807 Basi Revolt and thriving high-quality coffee plantations.

towns.name: Pinili
towns.title: Land of Abel Weaving & Magdalena Gamayo
towns.description: Home of National Living Treasure (Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan) Magdalena Gamayo and traditional Inabel weaving.

towns.name: San Nicolas
towns.title: Pottery & Damili Heritage Capital
towns.description: Town famed for ancient terracotta pottery making (Damili) and commercial shopping centers.

towns.name: Sarrat
towns.title: Birthplace of Ferdinand E. Marcos & Santa Monica Parish
towns.description: Boasts the largest church in the Ilocos Region (Santa Monica Parish) and rich historical landmarks.

towns.name: Vintar
towns.title: Eco-Adventure Park & Vintar Dam
towns.description: Largest municipality by land area, famous for the Umok ni Siwawer nature park and zip-line adventure.

destinations.name: St. William's Cathedral
destinations.description: A iconic Italian Renaissance church built by Augustinian friars in 1612.
destinations.history: Constructed in 1612, St. William Cathedral is renowned for its Italian Renaissance architecture and its sinking bell tower located 85 meters away.
destinations.significance: Serves as the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Laoag.

destinations.name: Sinking Bell Tower
destinations.description: One of the tallest bell towers in the Philippines, sinking by an estimated 1 inch per year.
destinations.history: Built in 1612 on sandy foundation soil, its immense weight causes it to sink continuously.
destinations.significance: Historical landmark and popular tourist attraction in central Laoag.

destinations.name: La Paz Sand Dunes
destinations.description: A 85-square-kilometer coastal desert reserve perfect for 4x4 off-roading and sandboarding.
destinations.history: Formed over centuries by coastal winds and ocean tides, declared a National Geological Monument.
destinations.significance: Famous filming location for classic films like Panday and Mad Max style stunts.

destinations.name: Museo Ilocos Norte
destinations.description: Housed in a historical brick Tabacalera warehouse, showcases Ilocano heritage and ethnography.
destinations.history: Originally built as a tobacco warehouse during the Spanish monopoly era.
destinations.significance: Preserves indigenous and colonial artifacts of the province.

destinations.name: Paoay Church (Saint Augustine Church)
destinations.description: UNESCO World Heritage site famous for Earthquake Baroque architecture and massive coral brick buttresses.
destinations.history: Completed in 1710 after decades of construction using coral stones and sugar cane mortar mixtures.
destinations.significance: One of four Baroque Churches of the Philippines inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

destinations.name: Paoay Lake National Park
destinations.description: A 470-hectare freshwater lake rich in local legends and migratory bird life.
destinations.history: Legend states the lake submerged a wealthy village whose inhabitants were punished for vanity.
destinations.significance: Protected national park and important ecological sanctuary.

destinations.name: Malacañang of the North
destinations.description: A majestic two-story mansion overlooking Paoay Lake, serving as a presidential museum.
destinations.history: Built as the official residence for President Ferdinand E. Marcos during his administration.
destinations.significance: Features traditional Bahay na Bato architectural elements with grand wooden verandahs.

destinations.name: Paoay Sand Dunes (Suba)
destinations.description: Rolling desert dunes offering 4x4 thrill rides and sunset viewing spots.
destinations.history: Part of the extensive Ilocos Norte sand dune ecosystem along the West Philippine Sea.
destinations.significance: High-energy adventure hub for international and local tourists.

course_modules.subtitle: The Sunshine City of the North & Capital of Ilocos Norte
course_modules.description:
The Sunshine City of the North & Capital of Ilocos Norte


Laoag City is the capital and commercial center of the province of Ilocos Norte in the Philippines. Located in the northernmost part of Luzon, it is often called the "Sunshine City" because of its bright, clear skies and warm weather. The name "Laoag" comes from the Ilocano word lawag, which means light or brightness

Home of the UNESCO World Heritage Paoay Church


Paoay is home to the UNESCO World Heritage Site Paoay Church (San Agustin Church), a national cultural treasure. Beyond its iconic baroque architecture, the town supports farming and hosts the Malacañang of the North, a lakeside presidential museum.

module_lessons.title: St. Williams Cathedral
module_lessons.content:
Saint William's Cathedral, commonly known as Laoag Cathedral, is a Roman Catholic church in Laoag City, Ilocos Norte, Philippines. It serves as the seat or central church of the Diocese of Laoag. The current church was built in 1612 by Augustinian friars to replace a wooden chapel.


The first church of Laoag was made of wood and thatch when the Augustinians established the parish in 1580. The foundations of the current church were laid in 1612. It was damaged by fire in 1843 and was restored from 1873 to 1880 by the Obras Publicas under Engineer Antonio de la Camara and Father Santiago Muniz.


The church was occupied by Philippine revolutionaries in 1898, and later by the American forces in 1899. The ownership of the church was contested by the Aglipayans from the Roman Catholic Church from which the latter won ownership. The church facade was renovated by adding lime plaster in 1936.

It became a cathedral when the Diocese of Laoag was established in 1961. The church was again renovated from 1971 to 1972. It was slightly damaged in the 1983 Luzon earthquake.

module_lessons.title: Sinking Bell Tower
module_lessons.content: The church is also famous for its "Sinking Bell Tower", which sinks into the ground at a rate of an inch a year. It has survived several minor earthquakes since its construction, causing scholars to label it an Earthquake Baroque style structure. The tower, built presumably after the 1707 earthquake, has a foundation of 90 metres (300 ft). It is made of locally manufactured bricks joined by molasses and juice of sablot leaves mixed with lime and sand, and reinforced with four massive columns on each corner and a winding stairway leading to the belfry. It used to have a large clock on the tower's western face.

module_lessons.title: Paoay Church
module_lessons.content:
Saint Augustine Parish Church, commonly known as Paoay Church, is a Roman Catholic church in the municipality of Paoay, Ilocos Norte in the Philippines. It is under the ecclesiastical jurisdiction of the Diocese of Laoag. Completed in 1710, the church is famous for its distinctive architecture, a highlight of which are the enormous buttresses on the sides and the back of the building.


It is declared as a National Cultural Treasure by the Philippine government in 1973 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site under the collective group of Baroque Churches of the Philippines in 1993.


The earliest historical record of the area dates back to 1593, becoming an independent Augustinian parish by 1686. The construction of the present church was started in 1694 by Augustinian friar Father Antonio Estavillo and was completed in 1710. It was later on rededicated in 1896.


Some portions of the church were damaged in the 1865 and 1885 earthquakes but was later restored under the initiative of former First Lady, Imelda Marcos.
